pruned.rule: The register holds a source only when it can be collected. A source that did not answer the probe, and a source that was taken from documentation and never called, were removed. The register keeps a source that needs a key only while the key request is open and named in SOURCES.md section 8. ENTSO-E is the one such source.
pruned.now_note: `now` is the entry count on the prune date. The register holds 13 entries since the revision below. 11 distinct operators stand behind those 13 entries. Two operators give two entries each: Fraunhofer ISE gives /co2eq and /v2/public_power, and Elia gives the two value columns of one dataset.
pruned.record: SOURCES.md section 0.1 holds the probe result and the research of each removed source.

revised.why: A probe of the dataset that the entry named, ods192, read the title 'Production-Based CO2 Intensity and Consumption-Based CO2 Intensity Belgium'. The entry gives carbon intensity and not a generation mix. The dataset holds two value columns for one hour, and `basis` is not in the key of the record table, so one source id cannot carry both. The register now holds one entry for each column.

resolution_minutes_counts.counted_note: Counted from resolution_minutes_observed above. The three numbers cover the 34 countries. uk is the one country at 30 minutes. The eu aggregate is the 35th entry of that map, it sits at 60 minutes, and it is not a country.

measured_2026_09_17.method: One atlas snap over all 34 countries. The store records run_at 2026-09-17T12:44:30Z for that snap, with 28 countries. lt carries a curve from a second run at 2026-09-17T13:05:13Z, which makes 29. An earlier note said 15:44 UTC. That was the local EEST clock of the author, and not UTC.
measured_2026_09_17.horizon_hours_observed: 8.0 to 57.0, and NOT 17 for every country. at reaches 57 h with 229 points. Most 15-minute countries reach 33 h with 133 points. Several 60-minute countries reach 8.2 h with 9 points.
measured_2026_09_17.correction: horizon_hours 17 was measured on de, se and pl only. The horizon depends on the capture time and on the publisher's daily cut-off, and only then on the country. The store holds de at run_at 2026-09-17T10:20:51Z with 46 points that reach 11.4 h, and de at 2026-09-17T12:44:30Z with 37 points that reach 9.0 h. Both curves stop at 21:45 UTC of the same day. Derive the horizon from the returned array, and never from this field.
measured_2026_09_17.negative_values: lt carries 8 negative forecast values of 98, from -0.9 to -14.6 gCO2eq/kWh, beside a curve that reaches 81.7 g. The lt ACTUAL series holds no negative value. The collector drops the point and keeps the rest.

history_collected_2026_09_17.method: Full backfill of every country from 2015-06-01 to 2026-09-17, through the atlas collector. Counted on 2026-09-22, the `record_current` view holds 5,105,530 actual records from this source, and the `record` table holds 5,105,674. The difference of 144 rows is the superseded revisions. Neither number counts the captured forecast rows.
history_collected_2026_09_17.warning: A country in countries_verified returns a value for TODAY. It does not follow that the country has a history. Four countries do not.

thin.note: A thin country runs from its own first day to the newest day, and it misses days inside that span. It is not complete, and it is not partial.
thin.me: 3,527 of the 4,120 days of its span, which is 85.6 %.
thin.uk: 3,893 of the 4,128 days of its span, which is 94.3 %. uk is the energy-charts code, and the zone is GB.

partial.cy: 2015-07-25 to 2017-06-10 only, 27,198 records. 3,516 days still fail. Not usable as a time series.
partial.md: NO records at all. 2,981 days fail and 1,146 days return an empty list.

history_collected_2026_09_17.server_error_note: The API answers HTTP 500 for some periods and HTTP 200 for other periods of the same country. It is not a rate limit and not a size limit: dk for 2024 returns 8,784 points in 2 s, and dk for 2015 to 2026 fails after 17 s. The collector splits a window on a 5xx status and keeps the good halves.

sources.verification: GET /co2eq?country=de&start=2026-09-10&end=2026-09-11 -> HTTP 200, quarter-hourly. Twelve further countries probed, all HTTP 200 with non-null values.
risks: Undocumented: absent from GET /v2 (19 endpoints) and from /openapi.json (37 paths). Re-verified 2026-09-16.
No v2 form: GET /v2/co2eq returns HTTP 404 while GET /co2eq returns HTTP 200 with deprecated:false. Every other endpoint has both forms.
No published emission-factor table, no scope statement, no version.
Resolution differs by country. Resample before any cross-country statistic.
Almost certainly does not flow-trace imports, so a net-importing country is overstated and a net exporter is flattered.

MEASURED 2026-09-17: a country that returns a value for today can hold no history. cy, ge, md and xk are in countries_verified, and only xk gives a usable series. See coverage.history_collected_2026_09_17.
MEASURED 2026-09-17: the API answers HTTP 500 for some periods of some countries. A collector that makes one request for the whole history loses the whole country. Split the window on a 5xx status.

MEASURED 2026-09-17, found by the portal: ge sits at a floor of 3.0 to 3.9 gCO2eq/kWh for whole months. 8 complete months from 2022-05 to 2024-07, of 665 to 744 records each, hold a mean below 8 g, and the minimum of every one of them is exactly 3.0. No lifecycle factor table gives 3 g to a national grid, because hydro alone is near 24 g. Treat the ge series as a model artefact until a second source scores it. The next lowest complete month across the store is ch at 10.9 g, which is plausible.

rate_limit.note: MEASURED 2026-09-18: HTTP 429 with 'Try again in 277 seconds' after about 6 fast requests. The publisher states no number. 12 each minute is the choice of this program.

methodology.publisher_wording: The dataset is an updated near up-to-date history for the CO2 emission from electricity consumed in Denmark measured in g/kWh.
methodology.detail: Emissions of each power plant above 10 MW, with every plant below 10 MW counted as one plant. Production, consumption and exchange per hour. The 125 percent method for co-produced heat.

coverage.rollup: The country value is the mean of DK1 and DK2, weighted by the gross consumption of each area in that hour.

sources.verification: GET /dataset/CO2Emis?limit=3&sort=Minutes5UTC%20DESC -> HTTP 200, records for DK1 with Minutes5UTC timestamps. Re-probed 2026-09-18: one year is 210,792 rows and 24 MB in one request.
risks: The dataset DeclarationEmissionHour returned HTTP 404 'dataset not found'. It was renamed. Find the current name in the catalogue.
MEASURED 2026-09-18: the publisher writes 'Errors will occur, and will generally not be corrected.' A wrong value stays wrong in this series.
MEASURED 2026-09-18: DK1 and DK2 are not one grid. They held 57 and 24 gCO2/kWh at one instant. A country value needs the load weight, and a plain mean of the two areas is a different number.
The basis is consumption and not production, so this series counts the emissions of an import and energy-charts does not.
ElectricityBalanceNonv also holds a load column. The publisher discontinued it on 2026-01-06 and will delete it. Use GenerationProdTypeExchange.

sources.verification: GET /ods192/exports/json?select=datetime,production,consumption -> HTTP 200, 15,279 rows and 1.3 MB in one request. The field annotations give the unit gCO2eq/kWh for both value columns.
risks: MEASURED 2026-09-18: 284 rows carry production 0.0. The blocks repeat at 18:00 to 21:00 UTC on days that follow each other, which is a fixed local evening window. energy-charts gives a mean of 218.5 gCO2eq/kWh for those same hours and never below 82.4. The smallest value that Elia gives above zero is 17.4. A zero is an hour that the publisher did not compute, and the collector drops it.
MEASURED 2026-09-18: the series holds 15,279 of the 17,204 hours of its span. The largest hole runs 70 days, from 2025-12-10T18:00Z to 2026-02-18T23:00Z.
MEASURED 2026-09-18: the history starts on 2024-09-30. That is 2 years against 11 years of energy-charts. Compare the two on the period that both hold.
The publisher states no scope. The unit is gCO2eq/kWh, so the number counts more than CO2. It does not say lifecycle, and it does not say direct combustion.
The licence page renders from JavaScript, so the terms are not extracted. The catalogue metadata gives the licence name and the URL. Read the page in a browser before any external publication.
sources.note: ods192 holds two value columns for one hour. `basis` is not in the key of the record table, so each column needs its own source id. The two entries name one dataset, and each one makes its own request. `atlas/collectors/elia_opendata.py` holds the reason.
used_for: the basis gap, measured with the scope and the factor table held constant
